what: The four control arms. The two SemIf arms carry their requests; the two made from transfer-v4 records are listed by rule only (`provenance.derive`): `rebuild_requests.py --red-arms red_arms.json` restores them from the rebuilt requests and writes the four arms in the form the conversion scripts read (fixtures/red_arms.json), SHA-256 asserted.

header.what: the control arms the reference and the gates run beside the test requests: requests that change the state or the instructions of a test request (`base_id`, in requests.json) and move d1-3B's float32 answer by far more than 0.02 against it
header.rule: an arm is red when its probabilities move by more than 0.02 on some option against its base record's (the same question names) — on the oracle and on the graph; a graph that ignored the changed input would not move
header.selection: five candidate arms (seven requests) of another conversion's control file were measured on the provider's float32 CPU path, and these four requests were kept. red_not_paws_00 and tv4_000_with_state_of_tv4_001 sit near the line; red_word_tv4_000 (= requests.json red_arm_000, 'correctly' -> 'incorrectly') moves d1-3B by 0.0069 only, so it stays in requests.json as a record and is not a control here
header.request_sha256: sha256 of json.dumps(request, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(',', ':')) in UTF-8
header.record_format: requests.json's {id, source, request, gold, note, provenance} plus base_id and question (the question compared against the base record's same question); gold is null (an arm has no intended answer: the checks read |dp| against the base); provenance.derive = how the request is made from its base record

records.question: answer
records.note: MMLU: each question's options over the other record's question
